pins.name: GPIO0
pins.label: GPIO0
pins.notes: Must be HIGH or floating for normal boot; LOW at boot enters flash/programming mode. No interrupt support. Commonly wired to a FLASH/BOOT button on dev boards

pins.name: GPIO1
pins.label: GPIO1
pins.notes: Hardware UART0 TX0 — used by the Serial pfod connection, not available as a general GPIO

pins.name: SDA
pins.label: SDA (GPIO2)
pins.notes: Must be HIGH at boot. Commonly wired to the on-board LED on dev boards

pins.name: GPIO3
pins.label: GPIO3
pins.notes: Hardware UART0 RX0 — used by the Serial pfod connection, not available as a general GPIO

pins.name: GPIO5
pins.label: GPIO5 (Led Blue active high)
pins.notes: This board's RGB LED Blue channel (LED_BUILTIN) — active-high

pins.name: GPIO12
pins.label: GPIO12 (Led Red active high)
pins.notes: This board's RGB LED Red channel (LED_RED) — active-high

pins.name: GPIO13
pins.label: GPIO13 (Led Green active high)
pins.notes: This board's RGB LED Green channel (LED_GREEN) — active-high

pins.name: SS
pins.label: SS (GPIO15)
pins.notes: Must be LOW at boot (tied to GND via resistor on most boards)

pins.name: GPIO16
pins.label: GPIO16
pins.notes: RTC-domain pin: no internal pull-up/down, no PWM, no interrupt support. Commonly wired to RST for deep-sleep wake

pins.name: A0
pins.label: A0 (GPIO17)
pins.notes: Analog input only (A0) — cannot be used for digital I/O or PWM. Native range is 0-1.0V on the bare chip; no on-board divider confirmed for this board — check vendor documentation before wiring higher voltages
